predecessors.name: Satavahana dynasty
predecessors.text: the eastern Krishna River valley in present-day Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, where the Ikshvaku inscriptions are found (Nagarjunakonda, Jaggayyapeta, Kottampalugu, Gurazala, Rentala, Uppugunduru)

successors.name: Pallava dynasty
successors.text: the eastern Krishna River valley in present-day Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, where the Ikshvaku inscriptions are found (Nagarjunakonda, Jaggayyapeta, Kottampalugu, Gurazala, Rentala, Uppugunduru)

ledger.x: c. 227: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula founds the Ikshvaku kingdom at Vijayapuri. "Vasishthiputra Chamtamula, founder: c. 227-250 CE (Singh: 210-250)"; infobox "Established: Early 3rd century CE"; he "rose to power after Satavahana power declined". c. 325: the Pallavas conquer the Ikshvaku country. Rudrapurushadatta's reign "concluded shortly before the dynasty was conquered and eclipsed by the rising power of the Pallava dynasty"; the infobox dates "the Pallava conquest (under Simhavarman) and Abhira occupation of Vijayapuri to the early 4th century". c. 325: the Ikshvaku dynasty ends; "By the mid-4th century, the Pallavas controlled the former Ikshvaku territory, and the Ikshvakus may have been reduced to vassal status." The page does not describe the conquest.

wars.name: Pallava conquest of the Ikshvaku country
wars.outcome: The Pallavas displace the Ikshvakus in the eastern Krishna valley; by the mid-4th century they hold the former territory.

wars.name: Abhira occupation of Vijayapuri
wars.outcome: An inscription "dated to the 30th regnal year of the Abhira king" Vasusena was found at Nagarjunakonda; the page says the Abhiras may have invaded but "cannot be said with certainty".

certainty.note: No border is given; the extent follows inscription findspots in the eastern Krishna valley.
